title: Launch tracking commit lists items whose slice files stay uncommitted
lead: *Proposed.* Filed 2026-11-11 from the S312, S315 and S123 landings. When ork commits tracking edits on main before starting a run, the committed index must not list an item whose slice file it leaves uncommitted.
findings_note: 2026-11-11: S312, S315 and S123 passed their gates but every landing went red after merging main: slicer check reported "S345: marked as having a slice, but no file exists" and the same for S346. ork's launch commits a56c3f8 (S123) and d5880ab (S343) took main's whole `.slicer/index.json`, which held S345 and S346 from another session, but not those items' slice files.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
*Proposed.* `commitLaunchTracking` (`internal/engine/landdirty.go:104-131`) commits `.slicer/index.json` whole, with only the launched item's slice JSON and render. Another session's new items are in that index, but their `.slicer/slices/SNNN.json` stay untracked. Every later slice branch that merges main then fails `slicer check` at landing ("marked as having a slice, but no file exists"), and the run goes back to the implementer, which cannot fix main. Evidence: run land reports `~/.local/state/ork/runs/ork-20261111-215044-9784/land-2.md` (also the S315 and S123 runs); fixed by hand on main in 569d5d0.

Open owner question (Q1): what does the launch commit do when the index lists other untracked items? (a) *recommended*: also commit each listed item's untracked slice JSON and render, so main stays consistent; (b) leave the index out of the launch commit and pause the run with a reason when the item needs it; (c) refuse the launch with a reason naming the items.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `internal/engine/landdirty_test.go:19`: `TestLaunchTrackingListedSlices` commits S900 and S901 slice JSON and render when slicer list reports has_slice true; verify real git commit paths and remaining status. Independently vary whether S901 JSON or render is already tracked.
- `internal/engine/engine_test.go:61`: existing `TestLaunchTrackingItemOnly` preserves unrelated staged files. The listed-slices regression also preserves outside files, config.json, relay-roles.json, unlisted and has_slice false items, and edits to already tracked slices.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. `adj ask` Q1 and wait for the owner's answer.
2. Change `commitLaunchTracking` per the answer, with the test first.
3. Docs (*proposed*): `docs/design.md`. CHANGELOG.md: one bullet under `## Unreleased`.

Owner decisions (2026-11-12): How does ork learn which items the main index lists, so the launch commit can add their untracked slice files? (adj 321 is decided: commit-listed.) -> slicer-list: call `slicer list --json --lean` through the slicer client, take items with has_slice true whose `.slicer/slices/ID.json` or `.slicer/render/slices/ID.md` is untracked, and commit those with the item's own files. The owner's unlisted staged files, such as S05 in `TestLaunchTrackingItemOnly`, stay uncommitted.. The Check line `go vet ./... && go test ./internal/engine` is orchestrator-only. How should it be fixed? -> split: replace it with two lines, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./internal/engine`, each expected to exit 0. The allowlist in `internal/engine/perm.go:29` covers both, so the implementer can run them..

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go vet ./...` exits 0.
- `go test ./internal/engine` exits 0.
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `slicer check` and `adj lint` exit 0 in the worktree.
